newsitem.title: USA: Alabama lawmakers face education, welfare choices.
newsitem.headline: Alabama lawmakers face education, welfare choices.

text.p: The Alabama Legislature convenes its annual session on Tuesday with education funding and welfare reform at the top of its agenda.
Gov. Fob James has also proposed two major revenue bond issues, a $150 million issue to add computer equipment to classrooms, and a $700 million issue for highway and bridge projects.
The former would be paid from sales tax and other revnues earmarked for the Education Trust Fund and the latter would be repaid with existing gasoline taxes.
The state will have about $1 billion in general fund revenues to budget for fiscal 1998, compared to about $882 million for the current year.
James has proposed keeping higher education funding at current levels and using any new revenues to improve public schools.

That has already drawn fire from Frank Franz, chairman of the College and University Presidents Council. He is requesting a $58 million increase in the state's higher education budget, which has been cut by 6.5 percent in the last two years.
Lawmakers are also expected to propose new limits in welfare benefits and changes in the way doctors and hospitals are paid through the Medicaid program.

Medicaid, which is Alabama's biggest agency, provides health care to 630,000 poor residents. Last year, a dispute over the state's hopital payments held up $94 million of federal Medicaid funding. The dispute was resolved and the money released in August, but lawmakers said the program still needs fine-tuning.
